Training now writes durable, resumable I/O

T1, infrastructure (the unlock for logged runs)

  • Checkpoints: step-cadence (rotated to keep_last) plus never-rotated best.pt / final.pt. Only trainable adapter/encoder weights + optimizer state are stored; the frozen base is rebuilt from its own ckpt (strict=False).
  • Periodic eval cycle: evaluate() averages held-out loss in eval()/no_grad; best.pt tracks improvement.
  • Selection defaults to base_loss, not the total, because self-distilled shortcut terms can collapse to ~0 without real improvement, so they must not drive checkpoint selection.
All opt-in via training.output_dir; runs without it are bit-identical to before. Verified: 135/135 tests pass (CPU), plus a dummy-backbone smoke run produced correct checkpoint rotation, best-tracking, and load roundtrip.
This is the "we can now produce the first product-state row" slide. The eval/selection design directly anticipates the shortcut-collapse failure mode.

What anchor_prob is doing

D3, the shortcut training knob

Each training sample draws b ~ Bernoulli(p) with p = anchor_prob:

L  =  b · L_anchor                 # standard flow/diffusion loss at the finest step d_min
   +  (1 - b) · L_self_consistency

L_self_consistency:  s(x_t, t, 2d)  =  ½ s(x_t, t, d)  +  ½ s(x_{t+d}, t+d, d)
  • Why we need it. The anchor grounds the prediction in real data so the self-consistency target cannot collapse (to s = 0, or to a constant field independent of d). It pins the bottom rung; consistency then bootstraps the larger steps off it.
  • Why we will play with it. p trades data-grounding against few-step consistency: p = 1 is pure diffusion (no shortcut, the ghosted clip), while too-low p weakens grounding and risks collapse. 0.5 worked here; the paper uses 0.75. We will sweep it.

The positive control passed: shortcuts buy few-step robustness

D3, the important one

  • Image-only control pins step_level to the finest step and removes self-consistency entirely. Same adapter and plumbing, only the shortcut target removed.
  • It still beats the frozen base, but its few-step samples are visibly worse. The 0.5 shortcut run stays sharp. So the robustness is produced by the self-consistency training, not just a competent image predictor.
  • Qualitative, local run only: this is the smallest AVID model (only 11M parameters), no wandb id / ckpt / commit, so no metrics recorded (hard rule 8). Still owed: the MSE-vs-NFE curve for both arms.

Correction: actions are wired, but not effective

D4, reframing the action task

  • Earlier we assumed the shortcut adapter was step-level only. That was wrong: the AVID config already declares the act condition, the adapter UNet is natively action_conditioned: True, and a_t reaches its action head.
  • Yet predicted dynamics still look somewhat random / not action-following locally. So this is a diagnose-why task, not an add-wiring task.

Leading suspects

  • Frame stride too small: consecutive frames barely move, so the per-frame delta action is too fine-grained to displace the prediction (its own open decision).
  • Undertraining: small data + small batch (local); the sharp 0.5 figure came from this same action-wired config.

To rule out

Actions null/dropped at train or eval; a_t not held fixed across the self-consistency micro-step (would make the target ill-defined).

Status & open calls

still pre-results, now instrumented

  • Framework is broad and internally consistent; this week added the I/O backbone that lets the first real run be captured, and the multimodal adapter is now built (ready to train).
  • First D3 sanity check is positive: shortcut training visibly helps few-step rollout vs an image-only control.
  • No completed run with logged outputs yet; product-state results table stays empty by design (no number without a run citation). The gap is now squarely scale/compute.
  • ⚖️ Open decision, shortcut-collapse mitigation: anchor + warmup chosen as primary; whether the g(d→0) gate is ever needed stays open pending training evidence.
  • ⚖️ Open decision, frame stride: raise k above the current default of 4 (and sweep it) so a single action visibly drives the dynamics; bounded by length · k ≤ 300.
  • ⚖️ Open decision, output format: affine (scale+shift) vs direct delta. Framework built; needs the run to decide.

Next steps

turn sanity checks into sourced evidence

  1. Snellius (HPC) run, more data and bigger batch, to produce the sourced MSE-vs-NFE curve for both arms (shortcut 0.5 vs anchor-only 1.0). The first real product-state row. (D3)
  2. Diagnose action effectiveness at scale on the same run; if dynamics stay random, fall back to the null-action / fixed-a_t-across-micro-step diagnostics. (D4)
  3. Increase the frame stride for more dynamic clips. At the current stride consecutive frames barely move, so a single action is too fine-grained to visibly steer the prediction. A larger stride gives each action more displacement to act on, making action-following observable. (D2/D4)
  4. Land the anchor-step warmup (~20 LoC + 1 test + 2 YAML edits) so the first shortcut run is protected through the early transient. (D3)
  5. Train the multimodal adapter, now built: coupled video + proprioception dynamics, the hedge path if D3/D4 underdelivers. (hedge / D4)
